title: Largest Element in an Array
stepTitle: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
category: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
problemStatement: Return the maximum element of an array.
intuition: Sorting gives the answer but throws away work: you only need the running maximum, which one pass maintains in O(1) memory.

approaches.title: Brute: sort then take last
approaches.idea: Sorting fully orders the array when you only asked for one element.
approaches.code:
def largest_sorted(a: list[int]) -> int:
    return sorted(a)[-1]
limitations: Wasteful when n is large and you need only one value

approaches.title: Optimal: running maximum
approaches.idea: Carry the best-so-far; every element is compared once.
approaches.dryRun:
a=[3,8,1,8]
best=3
x=8 -> best=8
x=1 -> best=8
x=8 -> best=8 (strict >)
answer 8
approaches.whyWorks: Invariant: after processing prefix a[0..i], best == max(a[0..i]).

commonMistakes: Initialising best = 0 instead of a[0] — breaks on all-negative input
Sorting when a single pass suffices
patternRecognition: "Best/extreme value" over a sequence -> maintain a running accumulator
followUps: Return the index of the maximum instead of the value
Find max and min in a single pass with ~1.5n comparisons
What changes if the array is a stream you can only read once?
interviewInsight: This is a warm-up: they are checking that you reject the sort-based answer and justify O(1) space.
